page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-8xCPU-16GB is a Cloud Native family virtual server running on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC 7542 processor operating at 2.0 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 8 vCPUs with shared CPU allocation, 8 physical cores, and 1.0 thread per core. It is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing 2.0 GB of RAM per core. This server does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, but it comes with one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results indicate a split performance profile. In stress-ng testing, single-core CPU performance is poor, falling into the bottom 10% with a score of 781.19, while multi-core performance is weak at 6000.74. Memory bandwidth for large blocks is also weak, measuring 30.23 GB/sec for read-only and 17.66 GB/sec for write operations. However, the server achieves average performance in Geekbench tests, with a single-core score of 1282.0 and a multi-core score of 6083.0. It also demonstrates average capabilities in software compilation and Redis SET operations, processing 11.14 million operations per second.

The shared CPU allocation model presents a clear tradeoff, leading to lower single-core and multi-core computational density under sustained stress-ng workloads. Despite these limitations, the server maintains average performance for text processing, image processing, and small-model LLM inference. It is suitable for workloads such as basic web serving, software compilation, and lightweight database operations, where continuous maximum CPU utilization is not required.
